question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x{y}^{2}+2}{6}, & 2\le x\le 4,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expected value of $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
The marginal density function for $Y$ when $0\le y\le 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{x{y}^{2}+2}{6}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+2x]}_{x=2}^{x=4} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(8{y}^{2}+8-2{y}^{2}-4) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(6{y}^{2}+4) \\  & ={y}^{2}+\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}+\frac{2}{3}, & 0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the  expected value of $Y$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot ({y}^{2}+\frac{2}{3})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{3}+\frac{2}{3}y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{1}{4}{y}^{4}+\frac{1}{3}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{7}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$
